summary: For an empty input, combinations(0) incorrectly yields no combinations instead of one empty combination. LazyBuffer::new eagerly probes the input and marks it done, causing Combinations::next to return None immediately. The fix initializes the buffer without consuming input, allowing the zero-length combination to be emitted. Reversing only this constructor restores that bug, detected by the empty-input assertion added to tests/test_std.rs::combinations_zero. Both regions occur exactly once in their respective Git versions. No tests were run.
expected_failure: Failed assertion None == Some([]) for iteration 0
